problem: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$ where $F(x,y)=⟨2x+{y}^{2},{x}^{2}+2y⟩$ and $C$ is the boundary of the region enclosed by the curve $y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}$ and the lines $y=0$ and $x=3.$
worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066044/assets/fafd281fc63fb276c9759fd84f722096d494aa3e3fe9441f43aa6ecd1f9dfda9.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}(2x+{y}^{2})\,dx+({x}^{2}+2y)\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=2x+{y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}+2y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le \frac{{x}^{2}}{3}}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(2x+{y}^{2})\,dx+({x}^{2}+2y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x-2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}/3}(2x-2y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[2xy-{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{{x}^{2}/3}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{9})dx \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{4}}{6}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{45}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{(3)^{4}}{6}-\frac{(3)^{5}}{45} \\  & =\frac{27}{2}-\frac{27}{5} \\  & =\frac{81}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
